utterances.text: The document is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. So I want to say that obviously there was a house that was identified during the previous trial because this house that has a balcony, second house on Pionirska, so this house was identified. We see the marking, and the Defence is trying to confuse the witness at the moment because here this person did identify her house and from her house she said where the smoke came from. Now, if we want to have additional information, we should go to the transcript. Let me remind you that this witness, as you notice, suffered great trauma. All this happened almost 20 years ago so -- all this is very human. Obviously she did identify her house which means she did identify Pionirska, and if we can move to the transcript, if Defence wants to, we can do that. But I don't believe that the Defence can say that the witness was not able to identify her house or the house where the fire was, her second house, because she did identify places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo, you have made your point. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Shall we look at the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Or are you satisfied now that the witness has identified her house?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually I'm not satisfied. The reason I'm not satisfied simply is because what she had marked on the original exhibit was not the point. The original exhibit has no markings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The transcript, Your Honour, is page 1021 of the Vasiljevic trial transcript, in English only, of course. And it has been uploaded as 1D00-0635. And actually I misspoke on the page number, Your Honour, it's actually page 1024. And we're still looking at, I think, 109 -- there you go. And, Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That transcript I am told was in closed session so we should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Just looking at that, though, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us move into private session first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So do we have the page and the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's page 1024 and it basically begins at line 13 and the question and the answer is on line 18 and it's -- the witness states: "A. Yes, of course I did." And that was with regards to hearing activity outside the house. "It was nearby. I'm sorry, I'm unable to show you the house where this was happening. My mind was going, and forgive me for this. I was full of fear."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So your contention is that she did not identify the house --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- originally and she said the reason is that she was full of fear. She's not now full of fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I took it in context that she wasn't in fear at the time of the testimony but that it was actually the fear at the time of the incident that kept her from being able to recall that. The context, I guess, is open to debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, she had already answered and given the explanation, which is that she is now focused and she can think back more thoroughly. So that's the explanation. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go back to the photo -- and, Your Honour, just for purposes, since I will forget in the future if I don't, I would like to tender the previous statements of this witness. 1D00-0596 is the English version of the statement, the trial transcript is 1D00-0635, the proofing statement is 1D00-3144, and the aerial photograph that was originally referred to in the Vasiljevic trial is 1D00-0706, and we would ask that they be admitted into evidence at this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- and under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D00-0596 will become 1D18; 1D00-0635 will become 1D19, under seal; 1D00-3144 will become 1D20, under seal; and 1D00-0706 will become 1D21, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would like to go back and put the original statement which was, I guess, now being tendered as Defence Exhibit 17, which is the original statement, and I'd like to go to page 11 and also show the B/C/S version -- or excuse me, 18, and I'd like to show the B/C/S version at the same page of page 12 side by side -- excuse me, I apologise, actually, page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'd ask you, ma'am, to read the first paragraph in Serbian, please. Have you read that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court usher please move both the exhibits to the previous page, page 10, and move to the last paragraph, please, bottom of both pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like you to read the bottom paragraph, ma'am, please. Please indicate when you've had an opportunity to read that, ma'am, finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicated who was the owner of the house. I would like to have the name of the -- the name of the owner of the house be not indicated because we are in public session now. Witness V-115, you do not have to utter the name of the owner of the house in which you were residing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am -- ma'am, have you had an opportunity to read that bottom paragraph on page 10? So as you're walking to the place you're staying, you're walking; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: From what direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of my company toward the house where I was staying and in the direction of Pionirska, both up and down that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we have the exhibit that was 1D00-0706 which I believe is 20 or 21. And could the court officer please give the witness the device in which to mark up this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And with an arrow, please, of a short nature, please indicate from the direction you came from and where you were walking towards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you go all the way to the end of your arrow, ma'am, and turn around and come back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but it continues further up, outside the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I understand that, ma'am. So are you saying that when you were walking from your place of employment you came from the bottom of the photograph, as indicated, where you started the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went from the bottom up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the house in which you were staying that has the 115 and the little circle in it, that's where you needed to go that day, nowhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, tell me where you met with Mitar Vasiljevic on the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Yes, Mr. President. I think it would be necessary to go in private session because there's a lot of information that has been given which could identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, if we're going to be proceeding along those lines, we have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where did you speak with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I speak with Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true you spoke with a woman right before the fire, according to your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the woman on the street. She broke free from that convoy and she saw me, but I had no contact with Mitar Vasiljevic and it's right that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where did you see Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mitar Vasiljevic at the same place where I saw all these other people I mentioned and as I said in my first testimony, and I would like to ask the Trial Chamber why the gentleman keeps referring me to the first testimony if the accused was -- has been convicted. I'm now at this trial where Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic are the defendants. I shouldn't have to mention Mitar Vasiljevic. I thought this was done and over with. Why are you asking me about Mitar Vasiljevic all the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He's entitled to do so. He's trying to show that you're not a reliable witness. He's testing what we call your credibility by suggesting that in that trial you said one thing and in your testimony here you are saying something else. So that's the reason. Don't get upset about it. It's a legal strategy. It may or may not succeed. Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. Just one correction in transcript, this is page -- witness said, I will say in B/C/S [Interpretation] I was told that at this trial I'm not supposed to mention Mitar Vasiljevic. Or, more precisely, I was instructed that at this trial I would not be asked about Mitar Vasiljevic. We can listen to the tape also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true, ma'am, that you were instructed not to speak about Mitar Vasiljevic in this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-115 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct and don't take that literally. It was me who put -- spoke about Mitar Vasiljevic, but it was said to me that he is not important in this trial. So I didn't go back to the statements I had already given. Mitar Vasiljevic was not interesting to me and I was not -- I wasn't preparing to talk about him, and that's why I'm confused by your question why I was walking up Pionirska Street, why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I believe you are now belabouring this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where were the people moving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Actually I was reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I said you are belabouring this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Belabouring the point of the Pionirska Street fire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mitar Vasiljevic and what was said before. Are you moving on to a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long are you going to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Less than one hour, maybe more. I don't know yet. It depends --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In that case, we'll adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.
